- "w" stands for write. This mode opens a file for writing. If the file does not exist, Python will create a new file. If the file does exist, Python will erase the existing content and start writing from the beginning.

- "a" stands for append. This mode opens a file for appending. If the file does not exist, Python will create a new file. If the file does exist, Python will add content to the end of the file.

- "+" stands for read/write. This mode opens a file for reading and writing. If the file does not exist, Python will create a new file. If the file does exist, Python will erase the existing content and start writing from the beginning.

So, for example, if you want to open a file for reading and writing, you would use "r+".
